It seems that @Attila Gáspár and I have independently PR'd extensions to fun_prop that are very closely related: #42398 and #42516.
Thanks to @Michael Rothgang for noticing it. Would be good to figure out what is the best design here

I took a look at your PR. I thought about a similar approach with a custom simp set, but I initially dismissed it because it would require tagging the simp lemmas of almost every bundled morphism. Also, to work reliably, all the lemmas would need to be in unapplied form. But now that I think about it, this could be ensured by adding some preprocessing to @[fun_cast].

More precisely, we could add these preprocessing steps to @[fun_cast]:

  • For a lemma of the form ∀ x, f args x = ... , turn it into f args = fun x => ....
  • If the lemma is an equality of bundled morphism, then find a CoeFun instance and apply it to both sides.

This way, we could avoid adding lots of new lemmas. What do you think about this approach?

Also, maybe it should be called fun_simp or something similar, since it isn't about casts unlike norm_cast and similar tactics.

I wonder whether you have a more involved in mind - I was mainly thinking of getting rid of duplicated lemmas just for the sake of fun_prop working. Do you have concrete examples where the two preprocessing steps are needed to avoid new lemmas?

I was thinking of cases like Continuous (Equiv.addLeft x). Since Equiv.addLeft is just a wrapper around addition, it would be nice if fun_prop automatically unfolded it. This way, the autoParam of Homeomorph and other bundled morphisms could be just := by fun_prop. This would avoid both the use of dsimp (which is fragile and wouldn't work for IsAddApply) and making undesirable simplifications like eta_expand; simp; fun_prop sometimes does.

I realized that Equiv.addLeft is not a good example, because its simp lemma is ⇑(Equiv.addLeft a) = fun x => a + x. But it could as well have been Equiv.addLeft a b = a + b, where we would need this preprocessing.
Yes, I agree that these should be proved by fun_prop. If we do eta_expand; simp only [fun_simp]; fun_prop, where fun_simp has Equiv.addLeft a b = a + b, then this should work, right?

That would work, but then fun_prop would have to call eta_expand unconditionally, which could result in ugly goals appearing in the traces and error messages. This eta-expanding would also need to be done when fun_simp is used outside fun_prop.

If I understand correctly what Tomas Skrivan explained to me, then fun_prop already eta-expands. So I would expect that error messages should not change, but I haven't experimented with it. Maybe you know better than me how the internals work.
One idea for fun_simp would be that it automatically adds the theorem to the standard simp set, so that it avoids @[fun_simp, simp], because I would assume that you always want these lemmas in the standard simp set. I don't know how often you would want to call simp only [fun_simp] manually, maybe sometimes to avoid long simp only [..] calls.

It only does for the outermost function. But we would need to eta-expand every subexpression if we want to call simp on it. Also, in your implementation, the simp call is before fun_prop does the eta-expanding. Alternatively, we could call simp on every subgoal, but I worry that it would be slow (like continuity, which calls simp_all on every subgoal).
Yeah, I think that my current PR is not great, some form of eta_expand seems to be better.
I've implemented the preprocessing steps that I proposed earlier here. It doesn't have documentation or tests yet, but it could be useful for experimenting.

I've made PR #42959 with the proposed fun_simp tactic. I did some experiments using it for the fields of Homeomorph and so far it seems to work well. It still doesn't have tests, but first I'd like to ask for opinions on whether this is the right approach before writing them.
